# Bilingual Documentation Maintenance

<!-- Generated by repo-harness-builder; source: core/docs:3.0 -->

<!-- doc-role:canonical-ownership -->
## Canonical Ownership

`REPO-HARNESS.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, and the English files under `docs/repo-harness/` own operational facts. Spanish peers are complete reader-facing projections and link to their factual owners.

<!-- doc-role:translation-sync -->
## Translation Sync

Update the factual owner first, then update its Spanish peer in the same work unit. Equivalent meaning is required; literal heading or sentence equality is not. Locale-specific phrasing is allowed when facts, commands, paths, constraints, and outcomes remain equivalent.

<!-- doc-role:link-validation -->
## Link Validation

Keep one reciprocal language selector in each root README. Validate every relative link from the file that contains it and run `python3 .repo-harness/check.py` (`python` on Windows) after documentation changes.

<!-- doc-role:freshness -->
## Freshness

`CHANGELOG.md` is the sole chronological owner and `docs/repo-harness/current-state.md` is the sole current-state owner. Localized peers present those facts and identify the canonical source, so dates and status never become independent truth.

## Entry Mapping

In a list a reader counts, such as a dated `CHANGELOG.md` section, the Spanish peer maps one entry to one entry. A reader comparing the two must not have to guess whether a missing entry is a translation choice or a lost fact.

One exception exists, and it must be declared where it applies rather than inferred. A historical section may consolidate several English entries into fewer thematic Spanish entries only when every fact survives in some entry and the section itself says it is consolidated. An undeclared count difference is a defect, not a style choice. New sections are always one to one.
